verdict: Coinbase's revenue fell 22% from a year ago to $1.78B in a softer crypto market, and paper losses on the crypto and strategic investments it holds — $718M and $395M — turned a $274M operating profit into a $667M net loss.

takeaways.title: Paper losses drove the red ink
takeaways.text: The core business earned a $274M operating profit, but the crypto Coinbase holds as an investment lost $718M on paper and its strategic investments lost another $395M — together they turned a profitable quarter into a $667M net loss. Adjusted net income was $178M.

takeaways.title: Subscriptions kept growing
takeaways.text: Subscription and services revenue rose 13% year over year to $727M — stablecoin revenue alone was $364M — cushioning a 37% drop in trading revenue as crypto markets cooled.

takeaways.title: Cash covered the loss
takeaways.text: Coinbase ended 2025 with $11.3B of cash and equivalents, and still bought back $850M of its own shares in the quarter — the loss came out of a deep cushion.

oneTimers: A $718M mark-to-market loss on crypto assets held for investment — non-cash, and it reverses if crypto prices rise.
A $395M loss on strategic investments, including Coinbase's stake in Circle (CRCL).
Losses of $31M on crypto held for operations, also mark-to-market.
otherDetail: A $718M loss on crypto assets Coinbase holds as an investment, plus $419M of other expense — mostly a $395M loss on strategic investments including Circle — and $23M of interest expense.
footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. The quarter was a net loss despite an operating profit, so the slate 'Covered by cash on hand' block is the $667M net loss, funded from Coinbase's balance sheet. 'Other operating income, net' of $7M is folded into G&A, as on Coinbase's other pages. Figures are from Coinbase's Q4 2025 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-K.
